messages:
kai: Heads up — our canary that should be 5% is getting ~62% of traffic for the last 10m. Console shows split still at 5/95 though. :eyes:

maria: Whoa. Any obvious deploys around the time it started?

kai: Deploy-bot shows a rollout at 1769419800 (hashlib bump). Noticed surge right after.

ashok: I pulled the routing logs, sample: `route_assign user=U123 -> bucket=7 via hash(v='redwood_sid')` repeatedly. But hash distribution looks skewed. Snippet:```
# routing policy (simplified)
- header_guard: X-Client-Group -> prefer canary
- cookie_sticky: cookie=redwood_sid
- hash_based: hash(user_id) % 100 -> canary if <5
- fallback: baseline
```

maria: Wait hash(user_id) % 100 ? I thought we use modulo 1000 historically for fine grain.

ashok: Exactly. The PR changed the normalization from 0..999 -> 0..99 by mistake (was a refactor in the hashing util). That collapses buckets and makes ` <5 ` map to 50%+ of users in practice.

kai: Also noticed cookie_sticky still setting server group in the cookie when header_guard fires. Old sessions with `redwood_sid` kept mapping to canary because parsing changed. So two issues stacking: smaller hash space + stale cookie mapping.

lucy: Console shows intended config (5%) because it reads the config file, not real routing telemetry. Our rollout UI doesn't show live routed pct, just target split. We should surface live routed % next to the target.

maria: Agreed. Immediate mitigation: rollback the hashlib bump OR patch the normalization to use 1000 and flush sticky cookie mapping. Which is faster?

ashok: Patch is small — fix divisor to 1000 and publish a hotfix. But cookie stale mappings require a migration: set cookie expiry or add version in cookie so old format ignored. Quick patch: add a guard at top to ignore legacy `redwood_sid` that encodes group when not matching new format.

kai: I'll flip the patch to staging now. Can we gate it with a circuit-breaker? If anything weird, auto-fallback to baseline.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @kai at 1769422300 (hotfix/hash-normalization).

ashok: After hotfix, routing samples look back to expected distribution. Telemetry (sampled): canary routed ~4.8% over 2m.

lucy: Filed a small UX ticket to add “live routed %” + change history to Rollouts panel. We should also surface guard evaluation order in the UI.

maria: Postmortem notes: (1) hashing util refactor lacked integration test for modulo semantics, (2) cookie format change not versioned, (3) console UI missing live routed metric. Action items: unit test for hash normalization, cookie version field, UI telemetry.

kai: I'll open the PRs: hash-test + cookie-version. Assigning follow-ups to @ashok & @lucy. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident severity set to P2. Page on-call if regression occurs.

maria: Thanks all — great catch, small rollouts need live sampling on the UI.

kai: adding a quick script to reconcile any users stuck on legacy cookie format:```
# one-off to clear legacy server tag
UPDATE sessions SET cookie = NULL WHERE cookie_format_ver IS NULL AND created_at < '2026-03-10';
```

ashok: Will run in canary region first.
